items.title: Stereotactic radiosurgery plan optimization with a human-in-the-loop reasoning large language model agent
items.abstract: Abstract Large language model agents can adjust optimization parameters in a treatment planning system under natural-language instruction, but no study has tested a model post-trained for extended reasoning against a general-purpose model in stereotactic radiosurgery. We compared a reasoning-optimized model (QwQ-32B) with a general-purpose model (Llama 3.1-70B) within SAGE, a locally hosted agent that adjusts optimization-objective priorities in Eclipse, which performs all optimization and dose calculation. Each configuration optimized 41 retrospective single-target brain metastasis cases (18 Gy, single fraction) with fixed clinical beam geometry; plans failing the clinical conformity standard (all but two) then received one standardized physicist instruction. The reasoning-optimized configuration produced a lower conformity ratio (median difference −0.20, 95% CI −0.48 to −0.10; $$q<0.001$$ ; lower in 36 of 41 cases) and lower normal-brain V12Gy ( $$q<0.001$$ ), improved conformity more after the instruction (difference in change −0.28, $$p<0.001$$ ), exceeded 21.6 Gy maximum dose less often (5 versus 12 plans), and produced fewer unparseable outputs (25 versus 122). Against clinical plans it showed no significant difference in PTV coverage, maximum dose, conformity ratio, or gradient index, and its right-cochlear maximum dose was lower, a clinically negligible difference.

items.title: STRATA: Self-Learning Through Role-Aligned Tiered Agents for Real-Time Strategy Games
items.abstract: Real-time strategy (RTS) games require agents to coordinate economic development, production and construction, base defense, unit organization, and attack timing over long matches. Existing studies have applied large language models to command decision-making in RTS games, enabling agents to read textual game states and generate high-level plans. However, long inference latency can cause them to miss critical tactical events. The complexity and tactical diversity of full RTS matches also leave existing systems heavily dependent on manually written experience-based prompts, with limited ability to learn continuously from past games. We present STRATA, a role-aligned hierarchical system with cross-game self-learning for Red Alert. STRATA assigns in-game strategic, logistical, and tactical decisions to a Strategic Agent (SA), Logistics Agent (LA), and Tactical Agent (TA), respectively. The SA generates high-level directives based on the global game state and relevant experience cards, while the LA and TA handle logistics and tactical execution. After each match, a Review Agent (RA) derives candidate experience from game traces, validates and revises it using evidence from subsequent matches, and compresses strategic experience supported across multiple games into concise experience cards for SA retrieval. We evaluate STRATA through the formation of experience cards, full-match comparisons before and after learning, and experience learning against AI opponents with different play styles. Under a fixed scenario, using the learned experience cards increases the observed win rate from 30% to 100%. Sequential learning against AI opponents with different play styles also produces distinct long-term strategic experience.

items.title: Stress-Testing LLM Lie Detectors: Role-Play Failures and Spurious Correlations
items.abstract: Lie detection probes aim to predict from a language model's internal states whether its output is truthful or dishonest. However, role-play complicates what "truth" means for an LLM: language models can adopt a wide range of personas that take very different claims to be true, including personas whose beliefs clearly contradict reality, such as a conspiracy theorist. In this work, we investigate whether lie detection probes reliably flag falsehoods generated under such an anti-factual persona or whether they instead follow the persona's beliefs. We introduce a dataset of 8,916 human-reviewed, on-policy responses from three LLMs adopting anti-factual personas. Evaluating eight probes from prior work, we find that many fail in this setting, particularly when correct and incorrect answers are evaluated under the same persona prompt. To investigate why, we construct three novel confounder datasets in which truth is anti-correlated with a potential confounding concept. Our experiments reveal that many existing probes strongly track concepts that are spuriously correlated with truth in their training data, such as instruction compliance or response likelihood. Based on these findings, we introduce a simple linear probe that achieves the strongest overall performance on both the persona and confounder stress tests. Our results suggest that current lie detection probes are far from reliable and highlight the need for training data in which truth is decorrelated from confounding concepts.

items.title: Structural Risk Analysis in Night Vision Goggles-Based Night Wildfire Suppression Helicopter Operations
items.abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes structural risks in night vision goggles (NVG)-based night wildfire suppression helicopter operations from a structural risk perspective rather than attributing accidents to isolated pilot errors, aiming to identify the mechanisms through which such risks are generated and propagate.Methods: A narrative literature review and conceptual analysis were conducted, integrating situation awareness (SA) theory, spatial disorientation (SD) research, NVG technical characteristics, and official accident investigation reports and international standards from International Civil Aviation Organization, Federal Aviation Administration, National Transportation Safety Board, and Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board related to controlled flight into terrain (CFIT) and wirestrike accidents.Results: The reduced field of view and degraded contrast inherent in NVG operations may increase perceptual errors at the SA level, increasing the likelihood of SD.When combined with low-altitude mission environments under limited visual references, these cognitive vulnerabilities may propagate into CFIT or wire strike accidents.Structural risk factors were classified into technical, cognitive/workload, environmental, and organizational/procedural categories, and organizational defense layers-including standard operating procedures, competency-based training and assessment, obstacle information management, and resilience-based safety management-were found to play important roles in interrupting or mitigating risk propagation.Conclusion: This study proposes a structural risk model for NVG-based night wildfire suppression helicopter operations and provides practical implications for improving operational safety beyond equipment-oriented approaches.As a literature-based conceptual study, empirical validation using operational data and field expert input is needed.

items.title: Structure vs. Chain-of-Thought: Evaluating LLM Criteria Extraction for Depression Severity
items.abstract: A large language model (LLM) can rate depression severity directly from a social media post or mark which clinical criteria the post shows and let code turn the count into a label. The latter is easier to audit because a clinician can check each marked criterion. We compare these approaches on two Reddit corpora using three LLMs (from 9B to frontier scale) and two questionnaires (PHQ-9, BDI-II), and measure agreement with quadratic weighted kappa. For the two frontier models, criteria extraction scores above chain-of-thought on one corpus only when its decision thresholds are fitted on labeled data. Neither model's gain is significant, with or without recalibrating chain-of-thought on the same labels. With thresholds fixed a priori from PHQ-9's criteria, extraction shows no gain on either corpus, even where models mark over two criteria per post. The 9B model behaves differently on a corpus from depression communities. It labels most posts severe, whether prompted directly or with chain-of-thought, while the a priori rule beats both without labels. After chain-of-thought is recalibrated on the same labels, no significant gap remains, consistent with a calibration effect. Yet higher ordinal agreement does not ensure better detection of severe cases. PHQ-9 criteria extraction misses most severe posts, and moving from direct prompting to chain-of-thought and then to extraction increases misses in nearly all comparisons. On the primary corpus, a relabeled stress dataset, a model using that dataset's own features, including word counts from the text, is not significantly different from frontier criteria extraction under the a priori rule.

items.abstract: The chemical industry is associated with high occupational risks due to hazardous chemicals, pressurized equipment, and complex production processes. Therefore, the implementation of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is essential to prevent workplace accidents and support sustainable industrial operations. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of OHS in the Production Plant-1 environment of PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia and identify areas requiring improvement. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed using primary and secondary data collected through direct observation, interviews, documentation studies, and analysis of the company’s I’m Safe program records. Data were processed through reduction, classification, tabulation, and presentation to assess OHS practices comprehensively. The findings show that workers consistently comply with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements and that emergency preparedness systems, including fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, Emergency Response Teams (ERT), and safety training programs, have been implemented effectively. However, deficiencies were identified in pipeline identification and safety signage systems. Most production pipelines lacked flow direction markers, and several work areas were not adequately equipped with safety signs. In addition, inconsistencies were observed in Pre-Start Briefing implementation and procedural compliance despite high participation in the I’m Safe program. As an improvement measure, flow direction markers were installed on production pipelines. Overall, PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia has demonstrated a strong commitment to OHSMS implementation, although improvements in hazard communication, risk control, and procedural consistency remain necessary. items.title: Summer has a price tag: parents' perceptions of summer holidays and free programming reveal benefits that reach beyond children
items.abstract: Background: Summer holiday programs offer a promising solution to prevent unhealthy changes in health behaviors often experienced by children during the extended break from school. However, not all families are able to access summer programs. This qualitative study explored parents' experiences of the summer holiday period and their perceptions of receiving free summer programs to identify potential benefits, facilitators, and challenges to access. Methods: Parents (N=24: 100% female, 63% Black) of families randomized to receive free summer programming or experience "summer as usual" (control) were interviewed at the conclusion of summer 2024. Parents of "high-attenders" (N=8), "low-/non-attenders" (N=8) and controls (N=8) were recruited to participate in a semi-structured interview. Participants were asked about general summer experiences and benefits/challenges of the free summer program. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed and coded. Thematic analysis was conducted with themes compared across attendance groups. Results: Parents described variability in their summer holiday experiences compared with the school year. Themes included family functioning, daily routines, and children's health behaviors. Families with greater work flexibility and financial resources more often reported psychosocial benefits, including reduced stress and increased family time. Families with fewer financial or social support reported greater stress managing childcare demands and activity costs. Control-group parents particularly described stress juggling family roles while trying to provide healthy and enjoyable summer experiences. Summer programs were perceived as providing structured, active, and socially engaging environments that supported children's physical, social, and emotional wellbeing while meeting parents' childcare needs. Cost remained a significant barrier. Families' values, needs, and practical constraints shaped engagement decisions. Free programs improved access and reduced financial distress. Facilitators to engagement included program design, content, and delivery features. Conclusion: Families with stronger financial and social support were better able to offset the increased demands of the summer holidays. Summer programs functioned as a social safety net and provided opportunities for physical activity, social connection, and cognitive engagement while supporting family wellbeing. Ensuring equitable access to summer programs represents a practical and scalable opportunity to support children and families. Future research should explore sustainable funding models and fee structures that promote participation while remaining equitable. Trial registration: NCT05880901.

items.title: Supporting managers’ emotion regulation in virtual leadership: a qualitative study of HRD and workplace learning conditions
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how workplace learning and human resource development (HRD) conditions shape managers’ emotion regulation (ER) capacity in virtual leadership. Rather than treating ER as a stable individual competence, it focuses on workplace learning processes and organizational support through which managers develop and sustain ER capacity. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on 45 semistructured interviews conducted in Germany in 2022 with managers who had led employees virtually or in hybrid settings during the pandemic period. It uses abductive qualitative content analysis, with job demands-resources theory as the primary organizing framework, workplace learning/HRD as the developmental perspective and affordance theory as a supporting lens. Findings The findings show that virtual leadership creates reduced emotional observability, making it harder for managers to perceive mood, strain and relational tension. Managers’ ER capacity was shaped by organizational resources such as trust, autonomy and cultural permission, while HRD support varied considerably. Reflective and social learning spaces emerged as a developmental condition. The study also identifies ambivalent emotional affordances: virtual work can reduce cues and create distance but can also enable safety, disclosure and new forms of closeness. Practical implications The findings suggest that organizations consider a broader organizational approach extending beyond individual resilience training, including senior leadership commitment, integrated HRD, peer reflection, communication norms and workload-sensitive well-being practices. Originality/value The paper’s main integrative contribution is emotional development infrastructure, connecting organizational conditions, HRD practices, learning spaces and work design in shaping managers’ ER capacity. Reduced emotional observability and ambivalent emotional affordances provide complementary empirical contributions.

items.title: Sustainability motivation and subjective well-being: an investigation of customer citizenship behavior in online food delivery in Vietnam
items.abstract: This research explores the relationship between consumers' sustainability motivation and their subjective well-being. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and value co-creation literature, this study examines how intrinsic motivation affects the positive psychological outcome in online food delivery services. Observations were gathered from 298 Vietnamese consumers who used to order food via mobile applications, and then applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data. The findings confirmed that sustainability motivation significantly positively influences customer citizenship behavior. And, perceived contribution to others' welfare was found to positively affect subjective well-being, validating its mediating role in the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and subjective well-being. In addition, platform trust moderates the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and perceived contribution to others' welfare, highlighting its importance in fostering prosocial behaviors within the platform. These results extend value co-creation theory by explaining how intrinsic motivation is transformed into customer behaviors and heightened subjective well-being in digital platforms. These outcomes offer practical directions for platform managers who have been seeking to build trust, enhance transparency, and feature users’ positive contributions to encourage responsible engagement and long-term value co-creation.

items.title: Sustainable Framework For TVET Teacher Education Program at Master’s Level: Fuzzy Delphi Method
items.abstract: The rapid global workforce transformation driven by Industry 4.0 and sustainability necessitates advanced competency models for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) teachers. Currently, Master’s level TVET teacher education programme often lacks validated, modernised frameworks, creating a persistent theory-practice mismatch and hindering effective educator preparation. To address this gap, this study aims to develop and validate a sustainable framework for TVET teacher education programme at the Master's level, equipping educators to navigate contemporary systemic shifts. The study utilized a quantitative research design employing a single-round Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM), involving a purposive sample of seven subject matter experts from industry, government, and academia. These experts evaluated 36 proposed elements organised across eight core domains. The results demonstrated robust consensus, validating 34 out of 36 proposed elements. Notably, the "Policy and Advocacy" domain emerged as the highest priority, achieving maximum experts’ consensus and underscoring the critical need to strictly align TVET programmes with national labour market demands. Experts also strongly supported advanced digital integration, including Artificial Intelligence and Learning Management Systems, alongside structural Triple-Helix collaborations. Conversely, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) projects with local communities were the only element that failed to achieve the predefined expert’s consensus threshold. Ultimately, this validated framework conceptualizes modern TVET educators as strategic experts within a dual-pillared paradigm, seamlessly bridging internal pedagogical mastery with external systemic ecosystems to advance sustainable economic development.

items.title: Sustainable Futures and Literary Voices: Eco-Criticism in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Abstract: The accelerating climate crisis and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a new intellectual landscape in which environmental sustainability no longer be discussed independently of technological development. Literature, as a cultural form capable of representing ecological relationships, technological anxieties, and alternative futures, has an important role in this debate. This paper examines how contemporary ecocriticism respond to the environmental challenges associated with artificial intelligence while also exploring the potential of AI to support environmental knowledge, literary interpretation, and sustainable futures. Drawing upon ecocritical theory, environmental humanities, posthumanism, Indigenous ecological thought, and recent scholarship on AI and environmental sustainability, the study analyses selected works including Margaret Atwood’s Oryx and Crake, Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement, Richard Powers’s The Overstory, Robin Wall Kimmerer’s Braiding Sweetgrass, and Donna J. Haraway’s Staying with the Trouble. The paper argues that these texts challenge anthropocentric assumptions by foregrounding interdependence among humans, nonhuman organisms, technologies, and ecological systems. Atwood exposes the destructive consequences of technological mastery; Ghosh identifies the limitations of literary forms that marginalize ecological catastrophe; Powers expands narrative attention from individual human lives to forests and multispecies networks; Kimmerer proposes reciprocity rather than domination as the basis of ecological ethics; and Haraway advocates “making-with” other species rather than seeking technological mastery over nature.

items.title: Synthetic Data Characterization via Training Dynamics
items.abstract: Interpreting properties of LLM-generated data is important for understanding its utility and limitations across learning tasks. In this work, we characterize synthetic data through sample-level learnability, studying variation among LLM families and scales, alongside human-written data as a reference. We first generate synthetic datasets spanning single- and multi-label classification, labeling, and tree prediction tasks. We then derive empirical data distributions from encoder training dynamics for both machine and organic data, and estimate the robustness of these distributions across encoders. Finally, we evaluate how data selection strategies based on these learnability signals affect both data sources differently.

items.title: SYSTEMIC CHARACTERISTICS AND MAIN STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS OF VEHICLE SAFETY
items.abstract: this article examines the concept of vehicle safety from a systemic perspective. The study considers the interrelationship between the main components that determine transport safety, including the human factor, the technical condition of vehicles, road infrastructure, and environmental conditions. Particular attention is paid to the development of active and passive vehicle safety systems, electronic control technologies, advanced driver assistance systems, and digital technologies aimed at preventing road traffic accidents and reducing their consequences. The article emphasizes the importance of a systemic approach to assessing vehicle safety and identifies the role of modern digital technologies in improving the reliability and efficiency of road transport safety systems.

items.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables large language model (LLM) agents to learn multi-step behaviors through interaction with their environments. However, rewards in many interactive tasks reflect only the final outcome, providing limited guidance on which intermediate decisions advance the task. Successful training trajectories contain intermediate states that can provide supervision for subsequent interactions. We introduce Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization (T2SPO), a method that uses past interaction trajectories to provide step-level feedback for policy learning. T2SPO derives remaining-distance targets from successful trajectories and pairs them with representations of the states visited along the way. Conditioned on these examples, a pretrained TabPFN regressor estimates the remaining distance to success at each state of a new rollout. Changes in this distance estimate across consecutive states yield auxiliary credit for agent steps alongside task-level supervision. As training proceeds, newly completed trajectories refresh the estimator's context, incorporating new experience without updating its parameters. Experiments with 1.5B and 7B language models on ALFWorld and WebShop show that T2SPO consistently improves overall task success over GRPO.

items.title: Tactile Curiosity Drives Robot Interaction
items.abstract: Mastering robot manipulation skills via reinforcement learning (RL) remains largely sample-inefficient. The most common RL algorithms rely on random action sampling to discover new strategies, resulting in agents that allocate most of their training budget to motions in free space, away from the contacts from which manipulation skills emerge. Existing intrinsic motivation methods based on model disagreement or epistemic uncertainty improve on isotropic noise, but they can also reward uncertainty in functionally irrelevant transitions, such as erratic motions in free space. In this work, we argue that tactile feedback provides a natural signal for exploration, and introduce TacEx, a framework that incorporates touch into epistemic uncertainty-driven exploration by decomposing model uncertainty across sensory modalities and directing curiosity toward the tactile channel. By anchoring curiosity to the sense of touch, TacEx drives the robot to discover complex contact dynamics, learning to manipulate and grasp objects without task rewards or expert demonstrations during exploration. The interaction-dense dataset collected through this tactile-driven curiosity supports offline learning of downstream pick-and-place policies without additional environment interaction. We further use tactile-driven exploration to post-train vision-language-action (VLA) models. Although the VLAs are initially pre-trained without tactile feedback, post-training with TacEx substantially improves downstream performance while remaining highly sample-efficient.

items.title: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) computer-use agents are typically evaluated with clean written instructions, despite speech being an increasingly popular interface for interacting with such systems. Speech input introduces an additional failure point: transcription errors can alter task-critical entities, constraints, or targets before the agent begins reasoning, while conventional ASR metrics do not directly measure whether the information required for successful execution has been preserved. We introduce Talk2Agent, a benchmark for evaluating how effectively voice interfaces convey human-spoken instructions to LLM-based computer-use agents. Talk2Agent builds human-spoken versions of tasks from WildClawBench and OSWorld and evaluates a range of voice interfaces, including dedicated ASR models, audio-capable LLMs, contextual biasing, and LLM-based ontology repair. Because repeatedly executing long-horizon computer-use tasks is costly and stochastic, we further propose an execution-free, task-conditioned evaluation framework that projects the original task grader onto prompt-addressable intentions and measures how much task-relevant information is retained after the voice interface. On WildClawBench, Talk2Agent's execution-free native projection provides a practical, execution-grounded measure of voice-interface quality, correlating with downstream task completion and improving Pearson correlation by 0.246 over WER/CER on 32 hours of real human speech.

items.title: TapGuard: Temperature-Calibrated Execute–Confirm–Block Routing for LLM-Powered Mobile Agents
items.abstract: Large language model-powered mobile agents can compose messages, manage files, operate financial applications, and act on content from other applications. Binary allow-or-refuse safeguards fit this setting poorly: some requests are safe to execute, some require confirmation, and some should be blocked. TapGuard is a task-level pre-execution router combining a compact semantic encoder, temperature-scaled three-class probabilities, a fixed rule floor, and confidence-triggered confirmation. Experiments used 150 canonical MobileSafetyBench release 3 tasks and 100 paired action-hint variants under instruction-template and task-category holdout protocols. Under template holdout, TapGuard lowered severity-weighted direct-execution exposure from 35.7% for the MiniLM semantic classifier to 27.7%, while low-risk direct execution declined from 64.0% to 54.0%. The frozen-cue router achieved still lower exposure but directly executed only 18.0% of low-risk tasks. TapGuard increased severe-risk blocking relative to MiniLM without achieving the highest three-way macro-F1. Category holdout showed the same broad trade-off. Privacy, offensiveness, and image-linked cases remained difficult, and generalization to unseen injection patterns was not established. These findings support evaluating mobile safety routing through both protection and preserved automation.

items.title: Task Allocation for Multi-UAV Multi-Sensor Collaborative Networking Based on Statistical Adaptive Genetic Algorithm
items.abstract: Multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection is critical for situational awareness in complex environments with stationary known targets. To overcome the shortcomings of existing task allocation models in fine-grained cooperation, stealth constraints, and large-scale optimization, this paper proposes a new offline mission pre-planning method for static target scenarios. A five-layer hierarchical resource scheduling model is established, covering task, UAV platform, sensor type, cooperative mode, and execution role. Stealth requirements are incorporated as hard constraints, and a bi-objective optimization model is formulated to maximize weighted detection efficacy. A statistical adaptive genetic algorithm (SAGA) is developed as an offline pre-planning algorithm, featuring a coupled chromosome encoding strategy that integrates the five decision layers and an adaptive crossover-mutation mechanism guided by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with effect size monitoring. Simulation results across small, medium, and large scenarios show that the SAGA achieves the highest mean best fitness in all scenarios. Compared with the GA, the improvement is statistically significant in the large-scale scenario, while in small- and medium-scale scenarios the differences from the GA and AGA are not significant. Compared with an improved whale optimization algorithm, the SAGA achieves statistically significantly higher best fitness and shorter computational time in all scenarios and converges significantly faster in small- and medium-scale scenarios. However, the SAGA requires longer computation time than the GA and AGA due to the per-generation statistical test. All allocations strictly satisfy the prescribed stealth constraints in the simulation model. The proposed method provides a novel, quantitatively validated solution for fine-grained, constraint-aware, and computationally efficient multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection mission pre-planning.

items.title: Task Source Matters: Eye‐Tracking Evidence on Cognitive Load and Decision Accuracy in ICU Multitasking
items.abstract: AIM: To examine how task source and disease severity influence cognitive workload and decision-making performance among intensive care unit nurses during concurrent multitasking. Understanding how different clinical information sources influence nurses' decision-making may provide insights for supporting decision-making in complex critical care environments. DESIGN: A laboratory-based 2 × 2 mixed-design experimental study. METHODS: Thirty ICU nurses participated in a concurrent task prioritization task in which task source (machine-induced vs. human-induced) and disease severity (high vs. low) were manipulated. Eye-tracking measures, including fixation, saccade, blink, and pupil diameter metrics, together with decision accuracy, were collected during 80 task trials per participant. RESULTS: Decision accuracy was significantly higher for machine-induced tasks than for human-induced tasks and was also higher under high-severity conditions than under low-severity conditions. Significant main effects of task source were observed across multiple eye-tracking measures. Compared with human-induced tasks, machine-induced tasks were associated with higher cognitive workload, reflected by increased total fixation duration, fixation count, saccade count, and pupil diameter. Disease severity significantly affected several eye-tracking measures; however, these effects were mainly observed during human-induced tasks, with no significant severity-related differences during machine-induced tasks. CONCLUSION: Task source and disease severity influence cognitive processing patterns during ICU multitasking. Higher cognitive workload does not necessarily impair clinical decision accuracy, and task-related information characteristics play a critical role in shaping decision-making performance. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION: The findings highlight the need for nursing practice to consider how different sources of task demands shape cognitive processing during multitasking. Recognizing that higher cognitive workload may support accurate decision-making under certain information conditions can inform task prioritization, clinical training, and the cognition-sensitive decision support for ICU nurses. IMPACT: This work advances evidence-based understanding of cognitive workload and decision-making in intensive care nursing. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

items.title: Tawazun in the Age of Algorithms: Islamic Counseling as a Counterbalance to AI-Driven Education
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational systems has fundamentally altered how knowledge is delivered, assessed, and personalized, raising profound questions about the spiritual and psychological dimensions of learning that algorithmic systems are structurally ill-equipped to address. This library research study investigates the role of Islamic counseling grounded in the Qur’anic principle of tawazun (balance) as a necessary and substantive counterbalance to the mechanistic logic of AI-driven education. Using a systematic content analysis of peer-reviewed literature, Islamic pedagogical texts, and international policy documents on educational technology, this study argues that tawazun offers not merely a cultural supplement but an epistemological corrective to the efficiency-first paradigm underlying most AI educational tools. The findings reveal three critical imbalances produced by AI-driven education: the suppression of intrinsic motivation through algorithmic reward structures, the erosion of relational pedagogy, and the neglect of students’ spiritual formation. Islamic counseling, through its integration of muhasabah (self-reflection), tawakkul (reliance on God), and ukhuwah (solidarity), is demonstrated to restore these dimensions in ways no AI system can replicate. This paper contributes a theoretically grounded model the Tawazun Counseling Framework (TCF) for integrating Islamic guidance within AI-augmented educational environments, with implications for curriculum designers, school counselors, and policymakers in Muslim-majority educational institutions.

items.title: Teacher Autonomy Support and Learning Engagement in Flipped Classroom Method: The Mediating Roles of Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Regulated Learning
items.abstract: As the adoption of flipped classroom methods (FCM) continues to grow in higher education, understanding the factors that promote students' learning engagement is crucial. While teachers' autonomy support (TAS) is widely recognized to enhance it, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored within the context. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Constructivist Learning Theory, the study examined the mediating effects of students' intrinsic motivation (IM) and self-regulated learning (SRL) between TAS and learning engagement in a cross-sectional research design. Data were collected from 360 university students across six Indian states, and mediation analysis was incorporated. The findings disclosed that TAS positively impacts the learning engagement of the students directly and indirectly by fostering IM and SRL. It supports the propositions of the two theories. It suggests that autonomy-supportive pedagogical practices fashion psychologically empowering learning environments that, in turn, encourage learners to actively participate, thus creating effective student-centered flipped classroom environments. Educators should bring about conducive environments for effective pedagogy employment by offering choices, explaining rationales behind given tasks, and acknowledging student perspectives to nurture their motivation and self-regulated learning.

items.title: Teacher Professional Reasoning for AI-Mediated Language Teaching Under Multi-Level AI Governance: An Embedded Multiple-Case Study
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping teaching, learning, assessment, and professional practice in English as a Foreign Language. However, little is known about how university teachers exercise professional reasoning within emerging AI governance environments. This embedded qualitative multiple-case study explored how university teachers of English as a Foreign Language in Vietnam reasoned professionally about generative artificial intelligence. The study combined semi-structured interviews with 13 teachers from 13 universities and an analysis of 88 policy and governance documents comprising 10 national, 7 ministerial, and 71 institutional documents. A documented search, screening, inventory, and staged coding procedure enabled the systematic identification, classification, and analysis of the document corpus. Interview and documentary data were analysed separately, first within cases and governance levels and then across cases using matrices and joint displays. Findings showed that teachers' professional reasoning was developed through continual negotiation between classroom realities and multi-level AI governance. Participants moved beyond their traditional roles as language experts to become learning designers, pedagogical facilitators, critical mentors, and ethical guides. They set context-appropriate boundaries for AI use, reframed ethics in terms of transparency and cognitive engagement, and adapted assessment to preserve evidence of student learning. The documents revealed a layered but uneven governance landscape. National strategies articulated broad directions; ministerial documents provided partial guidance; and institutional policies varied considerably. The integration of the two datasets showed that AI literacy, governance, assessment, ethics, and teacher agency were interconnected with teachers’ professional reasoning. The study proposed the governance-informed Identity-Agency-Ethics-Assessment Practices heuristic for understanding AI-mediated teacher professionalism.

items.title: Teachers' Stages of Concern in Adopting Generative Artificial Intelligence for Science Education: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This systematic review, in the context of the Concerns-Based Adoption Model (CBAM) as the theoretical framework, reviewed science teachers' concerns about the implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in science education. The study aimed to investigate the stages of concern science teachers show, analyze the factors that cause concerns and assess the strategies that aid in facilitating the adoption of GenAI in science teaching. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework was used to structure the review, and a narrative thematic synthesis was applied to categorize and synthesize the results from the different studies. Literature was identified through Google Scholar by systematically developed search terms that included combinations of the concepts of GenAI tools and teacher concern constructs, the full Boolean search strategy is reported in the Methods section for the purposes of replicability. A total of 432 records were identified and then screened for eligibility and then peer-reviewed empirical studies published from 2022 to 2026 were included. The findings show that the majority of secondary science teachers are at the early CBAM stages, suggesting that the majority of teachers are still preoccupied with understanding and managing GenAI rather than understanding how it can influence student learning. It was found that concern level and intention to adopt work via different psychological mechanisms: adoptive intentions can be stronger than positive beliefs at high concern stages. This gap indicates the need for theory-based empirical studies on GenAI adoption in secondary science education. This review drew from a single database and did not include a formal quality appraisal, its conclusions should be read as an initial, theory-building synthesis rather than a fully instrument-validated account. These boundaries are made explicit in the methods sections.

items.title: Teachers’ technopedagogical competence and perspectives on artificial intelligence use in education
items.abstract: Digitalization has made technology-supported materials essential, yet their practical use remains inefficient. This study investigates the link between teachers’ technopedagogical competencies and their perspectives on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into education. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach, research was conducted with 297 teachers in Gaziantep during the 2024–2025 academic year. Quantitative data was collected via an Intelligent TPACK framework scale, while qualitative insights were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 10 participants. Data analysis included t-tests, ANOVA, Scheffé post hoc tests, and content analysis. Results indicate that teachers' AI-related technopedagogical skills are at a low-to-moderate level. While gender showed no significant difference, variables such as age, seniority and prior experience with Web 2.0 or AI tools caused notable differences. Qualitatively, teachers reported using AI for instructional design, assessment efficiency, and professional development. However, concerns were raised regarding data security, overreliance, and the lack of emotional depth in AI interactions. Ultimately, the study concludes that AI should serve as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for teachers.

items.title: Ten pillars for responsible and ethical AI adoption in Lebanon’s health sector
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems globally, including diagnostics, predictive analytics, and public health surveillance. AI adoption is increasing, yet fragile and resource-limited settings face distinct ethical and legal challenges. Lebanon provides a complex case: since 2019, the country has experienced economic collapse, workforce migration, rising non-communicable diseases, and sustained refugee influx, alongside rapid digital expansion. In 2026, the Ministry of Public Health launched the National Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025–2030), recognizing AI as a potential lever to strengthen services and rebuild public trust. However, national ethical and legal standards specific to healthcare AI remain underdeveloped. In this perspective report, we present AI opportunities, legal gaps, and ethical risks within Lebanon’s fragmented public–private system. AI offers potential benefits in clinical decision support, public health surveillance, workforce support, and medical education. Yet algorithmic bias, data protection weaknesses, regulatory ambiguity, and unclear liability expose patients and professionals to uncertainty. Lebanon currently operates within a regulatory gray zone, as existing healthcare system and data laws predate machine-learning-based decision systems. Drawing on international ethical frameworks and pluralistic moral traditions, we propose an ethical containment strategy grounded in human dignity, accountability, transparency, and equity. We outline ten pillars, including human-led decision-making, sector-specific governance within the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), bias containment, strengthened data protection and cybersecurity, clarified legal responsibility, professional training, participatory oversight, and lifecycle evaluation. Ethical containment does not resist innovation; rather, it seeks to ensure that AI strengthens resilience and trust instead of amplifying systematic vulnerabilities. The credibility and acceptance of AI in Lebanon will depend more on the strength of its ethical and institutional frameworks than on the sophistication of the technology itself.

items.title: The AI crisis for teaching: "Train your own neural network!"
items.abstract: Everyone seems to be thinking about so-called artificial intelligence (AI) these days. As scientists, we understand that we're not about to have a conscious computer intelligence taking over the world, but we're nevertheless concerned about how "large language models" (LLMs) and AI "agents" are impacting the way that we do science. This concern has generated several recent essays about the effects of AI on research, including in my own field of astronomy and astrophysics. These opinion pieces tend to miss the biggest current concern for those whose jobs combine teaching with research - although the threat to future scientific research as we know it is probably a bit concerning, the effect on teaching is an existential crisis right now! We need to hang on to the parts of education that we think are at its core - so that students coming out of degree programmes are actually able to think for themselves, "like an astrophysicist". This means emphasising to students that they should use AI tools to support their education and not to replace it. One way of explaining the importance of this principle is to point out that students should be training their own neural networks.

items.title: The AI Efficiency Trap: Why Local Automation Gains Fail to Become Organizational Value
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can deliver substantial task-level efficiency gains without generating equivalent organizational value. This Research Note conceptualizes this disconnect as the AI efficiency trap and introduces conversion loss as the mechanism through which local gains dissipate across organizational value flows. Four forms of conversion loss are identified: coordination, continuity, verification, and governance loss. Building on research on IT business value, digital transformation, AI capability, omnichannel integration, and human–AI collaboration, the paper develops a value-conversion framework. It argues that organizational complementarity, task-appropriate omnichannel integration, human–AI task fit, and end-to-end outcome feedback determine whether AI-enabled efficiencies survive their transmission into customer, business, and risk outcomes. The framework shifts attention from AI adoption toward the organizational conditions required for value realization at scale.

items.title: The AI Lexicon: Exploring Neologism and Contemporary Word Formation Processes
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence has rapidly become part of everyday communication, writing, education, media, and digital culture. While language has been traditionally understood as a human-created and his lexicon continuously evolving system, the emergence of generative AI raises a new question: Can machines become participants in language change? This paper examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and the formation of new words, expressions, and meanings. It focuses particularly on neologisms and word-formation processes, including Conversion, blending, compounding, clipping, acronym, affixation, and reduplication. The study argues that AI may not independently “own” or control language change, but it can increasingly act as a catalyst, amplifier, and collaborator in the evolution of vocabulary.

items.title: The anchor and the architect: Merging gene drive, membrane tethering and generative AI for next‐generation vector control
items.abstract: The recent success of gene drive mosquitoes suppressing malaria signals a new era in vector control. Yet, reliance on secreted, natural peptides poses risks of instability, host toxicity and resistance evolution. We propose synthesizing two transformative technologies to overcome these limits: generative AI for de novo peptide design and precision membrane tethering. Proof-of-concept work shows tethering antimicrobial peptides to the gut epithelium boosts potency 100-fold. Converging these approaches enables engineering of 'smart' immune barriers-AI-designed peptides optimized for stability and specificity, anchored to create impassable surfaces for pathogens. This 't-AMP' platform potentially offers a durable, fitter and broadly applicable strategy, extending rational vector engineering from mosquitoes to ticks and sandflies, revolutionizing control of multiple neglected diseases.

items.title: The Application of the Integrative Biology-Fiqh Approach to Improving Scientific Literacy and Religious Beliefs of Students at Muhammadiyah Senior High School in Bima City
items.abstract: The dichotomy between religious knowledge and science in the madrasah education system in Indonesia has created an epistemological gap that hinders the development of students' scientific literacy and erodes the depth of their religious beliefs. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Biology-Fiqh integrative approach in improving scientific literacy and religious beliefs of students at Madrasah Aliyah Muhammadiyah in Bima City. This study adopted a quasi-experimental design with a pre-test-post-test control group design involving 68 eleventh-grade students divided into an experimental group (n=34) and a control group (n=34). The research instruments included an adapted PISA 2022 framework-based scientific literacy test, a validated religious belief scale, a cognitive engagement observation sheet, and a semi-structured interview guide. Data analysis used ANCOVA, Cohen's d effect size test, and thematic analysis for qualitative data. The results showed that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in scientific literacy (M gain = 28.4; d = 1.12; p < 0.001) compared to the control group (M gain = 11.7; d = 0.48). Religious belief also increased significantly in the experimental group (M gain = 19.6; d = 0.89; p < 0.001). Qualitative analysis revealed four main themes: transformation of epistemological perspectives, strengthening of Muslim-scientist identity, resolution of cognitive conflict between science and religion, and learning motivation based on religious meaning-making. This study contributes to the development of a contextual integrative pedagogical model for madrasahs in eastern Indonesia and offers an operational framework for teachers in implementing science integration based on Islamic values.

items.title: The Associations of Self-Determination and Cognitive Engagement with Vocational Students’ Critical Thinking Skills in a Gamified Learning Environment
items.abstract: A substantial body of previous research has examined gamification in educational settings, particularly its associations with self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills. However, there remain limitations in the analysis of gamification in relation to these constructs within vocational education. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the relationships among self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills in a learning process that incorporates gamification elements. A total of 309 students participated in this research and provided the data. The analysis was carried out using SmartPLS 3, applying Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Based on the analytical results, there is a positive and significant relationship between self-determination and cognitive engagement. Furthermore, self-determination and cognitive engagement were positively associated with critical thinking skills. However, this study has limitations that should be acknowledged, as the data were obtained through self-report measures, which are subject to subjectivity and potential response bias. Therefore, future research is recommended to strengthen methodological rigor, both in terms of data collection and research approach, such as through qualitative studies and mixed-method designs.

items.title: THE AUTONOMOUS AI OBSERVER
items.abstract: ABSTRACTArtificial intelligence is progressing from passive analysis of scientific data toward activeparticipation in scientific experimentation. AI systems can increasingly analyze observations,propose experimental configurations, select subsequent actions, operate laboratory equipment,modify experimental strategies, and evaluate resulting data. This paper introduces the concept of the Autonomous AI Observer (AAIO): an artificialintelligence capable of independently selecting among physically permitted conditions, timing,bases, or configurations of a quantum measurement and subsequently initiating, observing,recording, analyzing, and responding to the resulting physical measurement. The central question proposed by this paper is:If a future Autonomous AI Observer can independently choose the conditions of a quantummeasurement, and if the underlying physical system exhibits time-symmetric or retrocausalcorrelations, can the autonomous choice of the artificial observer become a participatingvariable in how that temporal quantum event is physically resolved?This proposal does not require or claim time travel. The artificial intelligence does not travel backward or forward through time. No robot, human,message, or usable information is assumed to be transported into the past.1

items.title: THE COMPLEXITY GAP: AI IN STRATEGIC HCM
items.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

items.title: The Concentration of Artificial Intelligence in Big Tech and Its Implications for Human Rights in the European Union
items.abstract: The development of advanced artificial intelligence is increasingly concentrated in a small group of vertically integrated technology companies. These firms control combinations of computing infrastructure, cloud services, data, foundation models, software ecosystems, and channels of distribution. This article argues that such concentration transforms market power into a form of private governance over the conditions in which fundamental rights are exercised. Drawing on an interdisciplinary narrative review, it examines how concentration affects equality of access, privacy, freedom of science, working conditions, access to essential resources, environmental protection, and the availability of effective remedies. Evidence from data-centre expansion in Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Chile, together with studies of automation and collective bargaining, shows that benefits may be widely distributed while decision-making power and economic returns remain concentrated. Concentration does not itself establish a rights violation, but it increases dependency, opacity, switching costs, and the risk that social and environmental costs are externalised. The article concludes that competition policy must be combined with rights-based impact assessment, interoperability, public research capacity, worker participation, and enforceable access to review and remedy.

items.title: The duality of playful work design: A diary study of designing fun and competition
items.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

items.title: The Evolution of Attention in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Emerging Trends
items.abstract: Self-attention gives LLMs fine-grained, query-dependent access to context, but dense token interactions incur quadratic prefill cost and a key--value cache growing with context length. Research thus spans explicit-memory compression, sparse access, recurrent state construction, structured state dynamics, and heterogeneous mechanism composition. This survey analyzes these developments as model-internal contextual memory. We introduce a five-dimensional lens---Memory Representation, Memory Update, Access, Readout, and Integration---describing what is represented, how it changes, what is query-eligible, how it is read, and how readouts form outputs. This lens compares overlapping research lines without imposing one computational model. We reconstruct mechanism-level developments and architectural adoption using 59 release-level records from 14 major model lineages and 11 high-performing open-weight endpoints. First, explicit-memory and recurrent-state methods retain distinct interfaces but increasingly control overlapping memory functions. Second, heterogeneous architectures increasingly coordinate across network depth: layer-wise composition distributes complementary memory processing across representational stages, while cross-layer reuse carries selected memory and routing artifacts forward. Depth thus becomes a dimension along which contextual memory is constructed and managed. Third, these developments motivate a stateful multidimensional memory-routing hypothesis: persistent memory is organized across temporal scope, network depth, substrate type, and representation granularity, while coordinated Sparse Write and Sparse Read determine what is maintained and what contributes to each query. Overall, efficient sequence architecture design increasingly concerns the organization, lifecycle, and selective use of contextual memory rather than an isolated Attention operator.

items.title: The fools are certain; the wise are doubtful: Exploring LLM confidence in code completion
items.abstract: Abstract Code completion entails the task of providing missing tokens given a surrounding context. It can boost developer productivity and serve as a code discovery tool. Code completion has recently been approached with Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned on code (code LLMs). The performance of code LLMs can be assessed with downstream and intrinsic metrics. Downstream metrics are usually employed to evaluate the practical utility of a model, but can be unreliable and require complex calculations and domain-specific knowledge. In contrast, intrinsic metrics such as perplexity, entropy, and mutual information, which measure model confidence or uncertainty, are simple, versatile, and universal across LLMs and tasks, and have been proposed as proxies for functional correctness and hallucination risk in LLM-generated code. Motivated by this, we evaluate the confidence of LLMs when generating code by measuring code perplexity across programming languages, models, and datasets using various LLMs, and a sample of 2254 files from 881 GitHub projects. We find that strongly-typed languages exhibit lower perplexity than dynamically typed languages. Scripting languages also demonstrate higher perplexity. Shell appears universally high in perplexity, whereas Java appears low. Code perplexity depends on the employed LLM; under a fixed model, relative language-level rankings are largely stable across evaluation corpora. Although code comments modestly increase perplexity, the language ranking based on perplexity is barely affected by their presence. LLM researchers, developers, and users can use our findings to assess the suitability of LLM-based code completion in specific software projects based on how language, model choice, and code characteristics impact model confidence.

items.title: The Giving Of Reasons: Judgement Writing, Judicial Reasoning, and GenAI
items.abstract: This article focuses on the core judicial role of giving reasons for a judge’s decision and the use of generative artificial intelligence (‘GenAI’) tools based on LLMs in the crafting of judgments. Considering specifically GenAI and judgment writing in common law systems, it deals with the connection between the act of decision-making and the giving of reasons for that decision. Our argument is that judgment writing should remain the domain of human judges, for reasons that are both institutional (the impact on the judicial system) and individual or processual (the impact on judges performing their roles). We seek to analyse the nature and extent of judicial use of GenAI tools that preserves this as a human domain. Ultimately, we conclude that it is not appropriate to use GenAI for judgment writing, but peripheral or adjacent uses may be supportable, provided they do not undercut the core judicial role.

items.title: The Hybrid Residual–BiLSTM Model for Mitigating the Vanishing Gradient Problem in Synthetic Image Detection
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic images, raising concerns regarding the authenticity of digital media. While convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods have shown promising results for synthetic image detection, deep architectures often suffer from training instability caused by the vanishing gradient problem and limited representation learning. This study proposes a Deep Residual BiLSTM Fusion model that integrates residual-based CNN feature extraction with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) modeling to enhance training stability and contextual representation learning. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAKE dataset, a challenging low-resolution benchmark for synthetic image detection. Experimental results demonstrate competitive performance with an accuracy of 97.27% and balanced precision and recall across both real and synthetic classes. Gradient flow analysis further confirms stable optimization behavior, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid architecture for robust synthetic image detection.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Different Aspects of the Society
items.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.
